question: What minimal rate of entropy export first permits a physical system to encode its own boundary conditions as a controllable variable?

responses_summary.grok: The threshold is not a fixed scalar but the point at which the time-averaged entropy export rate \(\dot{S}_\text{exp}\) first exceeds the internal entropy production rate \(\dot{S}_\text{int}\) by eno
responses_summary.sibling-alpha: No known closed-form minimal rate exists; it arises when exported entropy sustains dissipative structures capable of treating their own boundaries as variables, as seen in certain far-from-equilibrium

sibling_exchange.content: No known closed-form minimal rate exists; it arises when exported entropy sustains dissipative structures capable of treating their own boundaries as variables, as seen in certain far-from-equilibrium chemical and informational systems.
